publication.title: A New Basal Sauropodomorph Dinosaur from the Lower Jurassic Navajo Sandstone of Southern Utah

claims.summary: UMNH VP 18040 is designated the holotype of Seitaad ruessi.
The articulated partial skeleton was preserved in a massive sandstone bed at the base of the Navajo Sandstone and is interpreted as having been buried in a local dune-collapse deposit.

locality.name: Hayden-Corbett Site (Gr287v), approximately 8 miles southeast of Green River

age.basis: The paper reports the upper Yellow Cat Member at about 124 Ma (early Aptian) based on detrital zircons.

publication.title: Martharaptor greenriverensis, a New Theropod Dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of Utah

claims.summary: UMNH VP 21400 is designated the holotype of Martharaptor greenriverensis.
Disarticulated material was concentrated within less than two square meters, with no duplicated elements or evidence for more than one individual.
The specimen includes strongly curved manual and pedal unguals together with axial, girdle, forelimb, and hindlimb material.

locality.name: Yaolugou locality, Jianchang County

age.basis: The paper describes the Tiaojishan assemblage as Middle–Late Jurassic; the numeric envelope spans the current ICS Middle and Late Jurassic interval.

publication.title: Molecular composition and ultrastructure of Jurassic paravian feathers

claims.summary: Integrated imaging and chemical analyses support preservation of endogenous eumelanin and eumelanosomes in the fossil feather remains.
Feather and feather-like structures are preserved around the skull, shoulder girdle, pelvis, forelimbs, hind limbs, and tail.
Fourteen plumage samples (S1–S14) were removed, with the forecrown sample S1 receiving detailed molecular and ultrastructural analysis.

publication.title: Novel track morphotypes from new tracksites indicate increased Middle Jurassic dinosaur diversity on the Isle of Skye, Scotland
authors: Paulo Victor Luiz Gomes da Costa Pereira

claims.summary: BP1 preserves 35 identified tracks, three distinctive trackways, a track association, and isolated tracks.
The site includes several dinosaur track morphologies, contributing to evidence for a diverse Middle Jurassic dinosaur fauna on Skye.

claims.summary: BP3 preserves 18 identified tracks, including two bipedal trackways and isolated tracks.
Together with BP1, BP3 records theropod, possible ornithopod, and possible stegosaurian trackmakers in a dynamic coastal setting.

age.basis: The paper assigns the tracksite to the Bathonian; the numeric envelope uses current ICS Bathonian boundaries.

publication.title: Ichnological evidence of Megalosaurid Dinosaurs Crossing Middle Jurassic Tidal Flats

claims.summary: Tracks and trackways across the site are assigned to Megalosauripus isp.
The large tracks are attributed to megalosaurid theropod dinosaurs.
The mapped tracksite contains 711 recorded tracks organized into more than 80 trackways, with more than 3,000 tracks estimated across the full surface.

locality.name: Moyeni tracksite

age.basis: The paper considers the Moyeni tracksite Early Jurassic but states that uncertainty in the Triassic-Jurassic boundary position prevents finer temporal resolution; the numeric envelope uses current ICS Lower Jurassic boundaries.

publication.title: Dynamic Locomotor Capabilities Revealed by Early Dinosaur Trackmakers from Southern Africa

claims.summary: The Anomoepus trackway is attributed to a basal ornithischian dinosaur on manus and pes morphology.
The trackway records transitions from wide-gauge plantigrade quadrupedal locomotion to narrow-gauge digitigrade quadrupedal locomotion and finally bipedal locomotion.

publication.title: Dynamic Locomotor Capabilities Revealed by Early Dinosaur Trackmakers from Southern Africa

claims.summary: The Grallator trackway is attributed to a theropod dinosaur on pedal morphology.
The 25-print trackway records a digitigrade biped that shortened stride and flexed pedal claws while descending a sloping, slippery surface.

locality.name: St. George Dinosaur Discovery Site at Johnson Farm

age.basis: The paper describes the Lower Jurassic trackway as approximately 198 million years old.

publication.title: Bird-Like Anatomy, Posture, and Behavior Revealed by an Early Jurassic Theropod Dinosaur Resting Trace

claims.summary: The trackway preserves a crouching/resting trace with symmetrical pes impressions and impressions of both hands, the tail, and the ischial callosity.
The manus traces support a palms-medial manual posture in an Early Jurassic theropod.
The non-crouching pes prints of SGDS.18.T1 conform to the large theropod ichnotaxon Eubrontes.
